pr.title: Add FileCheck annotations to mir-opt/issues
pr.description:
This resolves a part of #116971 .

The directory `tests/mir-opt/issues` has only one test issue_75439.rs which should add FileCheck annotations.

Originally it was introduced in #75580 to confirm that there were duplicated basic blocks against or-patterns, but in #123067 the duplication was resolved. So FileCheck should ensure that there is no such duplication any more.
pr.author: Shunpoco

classification.name: MatchBranchSimplification
evidence: The PR is a test-only change, but it specifically enables and adds FileCheck assertions for the MIR output of the MatchBranchSimplification pass. The test emission annotation names that pass, and the new checks constrain the optimized CFG so that target basic blocks are not duplicated. This is reusable correctness knowledge for MatchBranchSimplification. Inspected source confirms it is a concrete MirPass implementation in match_branches.rs that rewrites switch targets and runs simplify_cfg as cleanup.

processing.reason: The PR is test-enablement only. Its historical distinction is structural MIR CFG shape: the older `MatchBranchSimplification` output duplicated successor basic blocks for an or-pattern, while the corrected output has both switch targets reference the same `bb`. The source `foo([u8; 16]) -> Option<[u8; 4]>` computes exactly the same result in both cases, so duplicating versus sharing a successor block is semantically value-preserving. There is no source-grounded wrong value transformation to encode: any pair differing on this input would require inventing an unrelated return-value change, which the task explicitly forbids. Therefore no valid `test_program_pair` counterexample can be constructed; the regression is FileCheck/CFG-structural, not a concrete semantic mismatch.

analysis.originalLogic: The `MatchBranchSimplification` MIR pass rewrites branch/switch targets and then runs `simplify_cfg`. For code matching or-patterns, arms that semantically converge on the same successor should be able to share a target basic block. The PR describes that the original regression test was introduced to confirm that there were duplicated basic blocks against or-patterns, and that the duplication was subsequently resolved by #123067. The supplied patch itself only changes the test expectation, enabling FileCheck and asserting that the two switch targets in `bb2` are the same `bb`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, the switch/or-pattern branch simplification produced duplicated basic blocks for or-pattern targets instead of reusing one block. The incorrect output therefore had multiple target entries referring to distinct basic blocks where the corrected MIR has both target entries refer to the same basic block. The added test constrains the corrected output by binding the target block id once and requiring the second target to match it, rather than merely checking that a block exists.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions containing or-pattern matching whose MIR reaches `MatchBranchSimplification`; the concrete regression input is `foo(bytes: [u8; 16]) -> Option<[u8; 4]>`, which uses `std::mem::transmute` from bytes to `[u32; 4]` and big-endian `u32` constants. The test is marked `ignore-endian-big`, so endianness-dependent constant behavior is outside the intended target domain.
analysis.summary: Enable FileCheck coverage for MatchBranchSimplification on or-pattern code so the optimized CFG reuses one basic block instead of duplicating blocks for equivalent branch targets. This is a test-enablement PR for behavior previously fixed in #123067; no compiler execution or reproduction is claimed.
analysis.trigger: A `MatchBranchSimplification` run over MIR containing switch/or-pattern target branches that converge to the same successor. The old problematic behavior duplicated those basic blocks; the corrected behavior has the switch targets share the same basic block id.
preconditions: The MIR diff must be emitted for the intended pass via `// EMIT_MIR issue_75439.foo.MatchBranchSimplification.diff`.
Remove `// skip-filecheck` so FileCheck assertions actually run.
Test uses or-pattern matching over data derived from `[u8; 16]`, `u32` dwords, and big-endian constants.
The test is skipped on big-endian targets with `//@ ignore-endian-big`.
pitfalls: Checking only that `bb2` exists does not detect duplicated target blocks; bind the target bb id with a FileCheck variable and require the second target to use the same variable.
A retained test name such as `issue_75439` or the old comment does not by itself prove which pass currently performs the transformation.
Do not confuse this test-only PR with the actual duplication fix from #123067; the test now documents the corrected CFG.
Do not assume endian-independent behavior because the input uses `to_be`; the test explicitly ignores big-endian targets.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a `tests/mir-opt/issues` FileCheck test with an `EMIT_MIR` pass annotation. Remove `skip-filecheck`. Locate `fn foo`, then `bb2`, bind the first target as `[[bb:bb[0-9]+]]` with `CHECK-NEXT`, and use `CHECK-SAME: {{[0-9]+}}: [[bb]]` to assert that the other target references the same basic block. This specifically checks absence of basic-block duplication while remaining tolerant of the numeric switch arm index.
